$comment: Which `environment` a `build.onTransform` hook is told it is running for.
Two compilers read every module. The Rust bundler builds the browser bundle;
`runtime/compiler.mjs` builds every server render — `dev`, `start`,
pre-rendering, and each deployed function. For a long time only the first
called plugin hooks, so a plugin rewrote the browser bundle while the server
read the original file. Any rewritten value that reached markup made the two
documents disagree, React discarded the server tree and re-rendered (#418),
and the only symptom was a flash of the wrong content — never an error.
Both now call the hooks, which only helps while both name the lanes the same
way: a plugin that writes `if (environment !== 'client') return` is choosing
one side, and it can only choose correctly if the two compilers agree on what
the sides are called.
Replayed by crates/ruvyxa_cli/src/plugins.rs (`plugin_environment`, the Rust
bundler's mapping) and by tests/packages/ruvyxa/plugin-transform-lane.test.mjs
(`pluginEnvironmentFor`, the JavaScript compiler's). A lane renamed on one
side and not the other fails there rather than in somebody's hydration.
`bundleTarget` and `platform` are what each compiler already knows about a
compile; `expect` is the `environment` string the hook receives. The Rust
column is keyed by its `BundleTarget` alone because the target implies the
platform there.

cases.why: The browser bundle. The only value that ever occurred before the server compiler ran hooks.
An ordinary server render: dev, start, pre-render, and the deployed function all compile this way.
A Web-standards runtime with no Node API. A plugin that injects a Node import has to be able to tell.
The server-components graph runs on the server. `react-server` is a resolution condition, not another host.

$comment: When a transform makes the two documents disagree. `ruvyxa build` reports
exactly this pairing — it asks the plugin whether it really produces
different text for the two lanes, and asks the route graph whether anything
that both renders and hydrates reaches the module.

cases.why: An unguarded hook rewrites both compiles identically. This is the default and it is safe.
The document is built from one text and hydrated against another.
A 'use client' route has no server document to disagree with. The demo plugin pairs the two this way.
A route that ships no bundle never hydrates, so nothing compares the two.
